cards.title: Cumulative Capstone Review & Practical Laboratory Guide
body: 4.1 Scientific Method and Laboratory Safety in Chemistry

Scientific inquiry in chemistry is a systematic method of investigating the material world through controlled observation, hypothesis formulation, rigorous laboratory experimentation, and data analysis.

To safely and successfully study the transformations of matter, chemists must operate in a highly controlled environment: the laboratory. Laboratory chemistry is fundamentally different from theoretical study; it requires active hands-on experimentation, precise measurements, and strict adherence to safety protocols. Before starting any practical chemistry experiment, a student must become familiar with basic laborat

In addition to safety, executing the scientific method in the laboratory requires utilizing specialized chemical apparatus. Each piece of glassware is designed for a specific purpose. For instance, beakers and Erlenmeyer flasks are used for mixing and holding liquids, but they are not accurate enough for measuring precise volumes. cards.title: Lab / review
cards.problem: Which of the following represents the safest technique to smell an unknown gas generated during a laboratory experiment?

steps.text: Inhaling directly over a reaction vessel can cause severe respiratory damage from toxic vapors.
The standardized safe method is to hold the vessel a few inches away and wave or **waft** the vapors toward the nose with a hand.

cards.answer: Use your hand to gently waft the vapors toward your nose from a safe distance.

cards.title: Lab / review
cards.problem: When reading the liquid volume in a glass graduated cylinder, at which position should your eyes be aligned, and which part of the meniscus should be read?

steps.text: Viewing from above or below causes parallax errors in volume measurements.
To get an accurate volumetric measurement, your eyes must be directly level with the liquid surface, and you must read the value at the very **bottom of the meniscus curve**.

cards.answer: Look at eye level and read the bottom of the curved meniscus.

cards.title: Lab / review
cards.problem: Which of the following subatomic particles is located outside the atomic nucleus and carries a unit negative electrical charge?

steps.text: Protons and neutrons reside inside the positive nucleus. Electrons revolve around the nucleus in shells.
Electrons carry a unit negative charge ($$-1$$).

Protons and neutrons reside inside the positive nucleus. Electrons revolve around the nucleus in shells.
